Pm

Pm
V6

Pm
V7
TAnd it cometh to pass, at the king of Israel's reading the letter, that he rendeth his garments, and saith, 'Am I God, to put to death and to keep alive, that this [one] is sending unto me to recover a man from his leprosy? for surely know, I pray you, and see, for he is presenting himself to me.'
Pm
V8
TAnd it cometh to pass, at Elisha the man of God's hearing that the king of Israel hath rent his garments, that he sendeth unto the king, saying, 'Why hast thou rent thy garments? let him come, I pray thee, unto me, and he doth know that there is a prophet in Israel.'
Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm
V12

Pm

Pm

Pm
V16

Pm
V17

Pm
V18

Pm

Pm

TAnd it cometh to pass, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth of the month, come hath Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he and all his force, against Jerusalem, and encampeth against it, and buildeth against it a fortification round about.
Pm
V2
TAnd the city entereth into siege till the eleventh year of king Zedekiah,
Pm
V3
Ton the ninth of the month—when the famine is severe in the city, and there hath not been bread for the people of the land,
Pm
V4
Tthen the city is broken up, and all the men of war [go] by night the way of the gate, between the two walls that [are] by the garden of the king, and the Chaldeans [are] against the city round about, and [the king] goeth the way of the plain.
Pm
V5
TAnd the force of the Chaldeans pursue after the king, and overtake him in the plains of Jericho, and all his force have been scattered from him;
Pm
V6

Pm
V7

Pm
V8
TAnd in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month (it [is] the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon), hath Nebuzaradan chief of the executioners, servant of the king of Babylon, come to Jerusalem,
Pm
V9
Tand he burneth the house of Jehovah, and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, yea, every great house he hath burned with fire;
Pm
V10
Tand the walls of Jerusalem round about have all the forces of the Chaldeans, who [are] with the chief of the executioners, broken down.
Pm
V11
TAnd the rest of the people, those left in the city, and those falling who have fallen to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, hath Nebuzaradan chief of the executioners removed;
Pm
V12

Pm
V13
TAnd the pillars of brass that [are] in the house of Jehovah, and the bases, and the sea of brass, that [is] in the house of Jehovah, have the Chaldeans broken in pieces, and bear away their brass to Babylon.
Pm
V14
TAnd the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they minister they have taken,
Pm
V15

Pm
V16
TThe two pillars, the one sea, and the bases that Solomon made for the house of Jehovah, there was no weighing of the brass of all these vessels;
Pm
V17
Teighteen cubits [is] the height of the one pillar, and the chapiter on it [is] of brass, and the height of the chapiter [is] three cubits, and the net and the pomegranates [are] on the chapiter round about—the whole [is] of brass; and like these hath the second pillar, with the net.

V18

Pm
V19

Pm
V23

Pm
V24

Pm
V25
TAnd it cometh to pass, in the seventh month, come hath Ishmael son of Nathaniah, son of Elishama of the seed of the kingdom, and ten men with him, and they smite Gedaliah, and he dieth, and the Jews and the Chaldeans who have been with him in Mizpah.
Pm
V26
TAnd all the people rise, from small even unto great, and the heads of the forces, and come in to Egypt, for they have been afraid of the presence of the Chaldeans.
Pm
V27
TAnd it cometh to pass, in the thirty and seventh year of the removal of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty and seventh of the month hath Evil-Merodach king of Babylon lifted up, in the year of his reigning, the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, out of the house of restraint,
Pm
V28
Tand speaketh with him good things and putteth his throne above the throne of the kings who [are] with him in Babylon,
Pm
V29
Tand hath changed the garments of his restraint, and he hath eaten bread continually before him all days of his life,
Pm
V30
Tand his allowance—a continual allowance—hath been given to him from the king, the matter of a day in its day, all days of his life.

V13

V18

TFor Mordecai the Jew [is] second to king Ahasuerus, and a great man of the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking good for his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

C1
Pm
V1
TA man there hath been in the land of Uz—Job his name—and that man hath been perfect and upright—both fearing God, and turning aside from evil.
Pm
V2
TAnd there are borne to him seven sons and three daughters,
Pm
V3
Tand his substance is seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a service very abundant; and that man is greater than any of the sons of the east.
Pm
V4
TAnd his sons have gone and made a banquet—the house of each [in] his day—and have sent and called to their three sisters to eat and to drink with them;
Pm
V5
Tand it cometh to pass, when they have gone round the days of the banquet, that Job doth send and sanctify them, and hath risen early in the morning, and caused to ascend burnt-offerings—the number of them all—for Job said, 'Perhaps my sons have sinned, yet blessed God in their heart.' Thus doth Job all the days.
Pm
V6
TAnd the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst.
Pm
V7
TAnd Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Whence comest thou?' And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down on it.'
Pm
V8
TAnd Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Hast thou set thy heart against My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God, and turning aside from evil?'
Pm
V9
TAnd the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'For nought is Job fearing God?
Pm
V10
THast not Thou made a hedge for him, and for his house, and for all that he hath—round about?
Pm
V11

Pm
V12
TAnd Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Lo, all that he hath [is] in thy hand, only unto him put not forth thy hand.' And the Adversary goeth out from the presence of Jehovah.
Pm
V13
TAnd the day is, that his sons and his daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
Pm
V14
TAnd a messenger hath come in unto Job and saith, 'The oxen have been plowing, and the she-asses feeding by their sides,
Pm
V15

Pm
V16
TWhile this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Fire of God hath fallen from the heavens, and burneth among the flock, and among the young men, and consumeth them, and I am escaped—only I alone—to declare [it] to thee.'
Pm
V17
TWhile this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Chaldeans made three heads, and rush on the camels, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped—only I alone—to declare [it] to thee.'
Pm
V18
TWhile this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Thy sons and thy daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
Pm
V19

Pm
V20
TAnd Job riseth, and rendeth his robe, and shaveth his head, and falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance,
Pm
V21

Pm
V22
TIn all this Job hath not sinned, nor given folly to God.

Pm

Pm

BLAM Lamentations
C1
Pm
V1
THow hath she sat alone, The city abounding with people! She hath been as a widow, The mighty among nations! Princes among provinces, She hath become tributary!
Pm
V2
TShe weepeth sore in the night, And her tear [is] on her cheeks, There is no comforter for her out of all her lovers, All her friends dealt treacherously by her, They have been to her for enemies.
Pm
V3
TRemoved hath Judah because of affliction, And because of the abundance of her service; She hath dwelt among nations, She hath not found rest, All her pursuers have overtaken her between the straits.
Pm
V4
TThe ways of Zion are mourning, Without any coming at the appointed time, All her gates are desolate, her priests sigh, Her virgins are afflicted—and she hath bitterness.
Pm
V5
THer adversaries have become chief, Her enemies have been at ease, For Jehovah hath afflicted her, For the abundance of her transgressions, Her infants have gone captive before the adversary.
Pm
V6
TAnd go out from the daughter of Zion doth all her honour, Her princes have been as harts—They have not found pasture, And they go powerless before a pursuer.
Pm
V7
TRemembered hath Jerusalem [In] the days of her affliction and her mournings, all her desirable things that were from the days of old, In the falling of her people into the hand of an adversary, And she hath no helper; Seen her have adversaries, They have laughed at her cessation.
Pm
V8
TA sin hath Jerusalem sinned, Therefore impure she hath become, All who honoured her have esteemed her lightly, For they have seen her nakedness, Yea, she herself hath sighed and turneth backward.
Pm
V9
THer uncleanness [is] in her skirts, She hath not remembered her latter end, And she cometh down wonderfully, There is no comforter for her. See, O Jehovah, mine affliction, For exerted himself hath an enemy.
Pm
V10
THis hand spread out hath an adversary On all her desirable things, For she hath seen—Nations have entered her sanctuary, Concerning which Thou didst command, 'They do not come into the assembly to thee.'
Pm
V11
TAll her people are sighing—seeking bread, They have given their desirable things For food to refresh the body; See, O Jehovah, and behold attentively, For I have been lightly esteemed.
Pm
V12
T[Is it] nothing to you, all ye passing by the way? Look attentively, and see, If there is any pain like my pain, That He is rolling to me? Whom Jehovah hath afflicted In the day of the fierceness of His anger.
Pm
V13
TFrom above He hath sent fire into my bone, And it subdueth it, He hath spread a net for my feet, He hath turned me backward, He hath made me desolate—all the day sick.
Pm
V14
TBound hath been the yoke of my transgressions by His hand, They are wrapped together, They have gone up on my neck, He hath caused my power to stumble, The Lord hath given me into hands, I am not able to rise.
Pm
V15
TTrodden down all my mighty ones hath the Lord in my midst, He proclaimed against me an appointed time, To destroy my young men, A wine-press hath the Lord trodden, To the virgin daughter of Judah.
Pm
V16
TFor these I am weeping, My eye, my eye, is running down with waters, For, far from me hath been a comforter, Refreshing my soul, My sons have been desolate, For mighty hath been an enemy.

V17

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm
V11
TFor, from the rising of the sun to its going in, Great [is] My name among nations, And in every place perfume is brought nigh to My name, and a pure present, For great [is] My name among nations, Said Jehovah of Hosts.

V12

Pm
V13

Pm
V14
TAnd cursed [is] a deceiver, who hath in his drove a male, And is vowing, and is sacrificing a marred thing to the Lord, For a great king [am] I, said Jehovah of Hosts, And My name [is] revered among nations!

Pm

C12

V1

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm
V6

Pm
V7

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm
V21

TPaul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, to the assembly of Thessalonians in God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Pm
V2
TGrace to you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ!
Pm
V3
TWe ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because increase greatly doth your faith, and abound doth the love of each one of you all, to one another;
Pm
V4
Tso that we ourselves do glory in you in the assemblies of God, for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye bear;
Pm
V5
Ta token of the righteous judgment of God, for your being counted worthy of the reign of God, for which also ye suffer,
Pm
V6
Tsince [it is] a righteous thing with God to give back to those troubling you—trouble,
Pm
V7
Tand to you who are troubled—rest with us in the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven, with messengers of his power,
Pm
V8
Tin flaming fire, giving vengeance to those not knowing God, and to those not obeying the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ;
Pm
V9
Twho shall suffer justice—destruction age-during—from the face of the Lord, and from the glory of his strength,
Pm
V10
Twhen He may come to be glorified in his saints, and to be wondered at in all those believing—because our testimony was believed among you—in that day;
Pm
V11
Tfor which also we do pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of the calling, and may fulfil all the good pleasure of goodness, and the work of the faith in power,
Pm
V12
Tthat the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and ye in him, according to the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ.
C2
Pm
V1
TAnd we ask you, brethren, in regard to the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of our gathering together unto him,
Pm
V2
Tthat ye be not quickly shaken in mind, nor be troubled, neither through spirit, neither through word, neither through letters as through us, as that the day of Christ hath arrived;
Pm
V3
Tlet not any one deceive you in any manner, because—if the falling away may not come first, and the man of sin be revealed—the son of the destruction,
Pm
V4
Twho is opposing and is raising himself up above all called God or worshipped, so that he in the sanctuary of God as God hath sat down, shewing himself off that he is God—[the day doth not come].
Pm
V5
TDo ye not remember that, being yet with you, these things I said to you?
Pm
V6
Tand now, what is keeping down ye have known, for his being revealed in his own time,
Pm
V7
Tfor the secret of the lawlessness doth already work, only he who is keeping down now [will hinder]—till he may be out of the way,
Pm
V8
Tand then shall be revealed the Lawless One, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the manifestation of his presence,
Pm
V9
T[him,] whose presence is according to the working of the Adversary, in all power, and signs, and lying wonders,
Pm
V10
Tand in all deceitfulness of the unrighteousness in those perishing, because the love of the truth they did not receive for their being saved,
Pm
V11
Tand because of this shall God send to them a working of delusion, for their believing the lie,
Pm
V12
Tthat they may be judged—all who did not believe the truth, but were well pleased in the unrighteousness.
Pm
V13
TAnd we—we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren, beloved by the Lord, that God did choose you from the beginning to salvation, in sanctification of the Spirit, and belief of the truth,
Pm
V14
Tto which He did call you through our good news, to the acquiring of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ;
Pm
V15
Tso, then, brethren, stand ye fast, and hold the deliverances that ye were taught, whether through word, whether through our letter;
Pm
V16
Tand may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and our God and Father, who did love us, and did give comfort age-during, and good hope in grace,
Pm
V17
Tcomfort your hearts, and establish you in every good word and work.
C3
Pm
V1
TAs to the rest, pray ye, brethren, concerning us, that the word of the Lord may run and may be glorified, as also with you,
Pm
V2
Tand that we may be delivered from the unreasonable and evil men, for the faith [is] not of all;
Pm
V3
Tand stedfast is the Lord, who shall establish you, and shall guard [you] from the evil;
Pm
V4
Tand we have confidence in the Lord touching you, that the things that we command you ye both do and will do;
Pm
V5
Tand the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God, and to the endurance of the Christ.
Pm
V6
TAnd we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother disorderly walking, and not after the deliverance that ye received from us,
Pm
V7
Tfor yourselves have known how it behoveth [you] to imitate us, because we did not act disorderly among you;
Pm
V8
Tnor for nought did we eat bread of any one, but in labour and in travail, night and day working, not to be chargeable to any of you;
Pm
V9
Tnot because we have not authority, but that ourselves a pattern we might give to you, to imitate us;
Pm
V10
Tfor even when we were with you, this we did command you, that if any one is not willing to work, neither let him eat,
Pm
V11
Tfor we hear of certain walking among you disorderly, nothing working, but over working,
Pm
V12
Tand such we command and exhort through our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness working, their own bread they may eat;
Pm
V13
Tand ye, brethren, may ye not be weary doing well,
Pm
V14
Tand if any one do not obey our word through the letter, this one note ye, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed,
Pm
V15
Tand as an enemy count [him] not, but admonish ye [him] as a brother;
Pm
V16
Tand may the Lord of the peace Himself give to you the peace always in every way; the Lord [is] with you all!
Pm
V17
TThe salutation by the hand of me, Paul, which is a sign in every letter; thus I write;
Pm
V18
Tthe grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [is] with you all! Amen.
B1TI 1 Timothy
C1
Pm
V1
TPaul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to a command of God our Saviour, and of the Lord Jesus Christ our hope,
Pm
V2
Tto Timotheus—genuine child in faith: Grace, kindness, peace, from God our Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord,
Pm
V3
Taccording as I did exhort thee to remain in Ephesus—I going on to Macedonia—that thou mightest charge certain not to teach any other thing,
Pm
V4
Tnor to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, that cause questions rather than the building up of God that is in faith:—
Pm
V5
TAnd the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned,
Pm
V6
Tfrom which certain, having swerved, did turn aside to vain discourse,
Pm
V7
Twilling to be teachers of law, not understanding either the things they say, nor concerning what they asseverate,
Pm
V8
Tand we have known that the law [is] good, if any one may use it lawfully;
Pm
V9
Thaving known this, that for a righteous man law is not set, but for lawless and insubordinate persons, ungodly and sinners, impious and profane, parricides and matricides, men-slayers,
Pm
V10
Twhoremongers, sodomites, men-stealers, liars, perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that to sound doctrine is adverse,
Pm
V11
Taccording to the good news of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.
Pm
V12
TAnd I give thanks to him who enabled me—Christ Jesus our Lord—that he did reckon me stedfast, having put [me] to the ministration,
Pm
V13
Twho before was speaking evil, and persecuting, and insulting, but I found kindness, because, being ignorant, I did [it] in unbelief,
Pm
V14
Tand exceedingly abound did the grace of our Lord, with faith and love that [is] in Christ Jesus:
Pm
V15
Tstedfast [is] the word, and of all acceptation worthy, that Christ Jesus came to the world to save sinners—first of whom I am;
Pm
V16
Tbut because of this I found kindness, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all long-suffering, for a pattern of those about to believe on him to life age-during:
Pm
V17
Tand to the King of the ages, the incorruptible, invisible, only wise God, [is] honour and glory—to the ages of the ages! Amen.
Pm
V18
TThis charge I commit to thee, child Timotheus, according to the prophesies that went before upon thee, that thou mayest war in them the good warfare,
Pm
V19
Thaving faith and a good conscience, which certain having thrust away, concerning the faith did make shipwreck,
Pm
V20
Tof whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I did deliver to the Adversary, that they might be instructed not to speak evil.
C2
Pm
V1
TI exhort, then, first of all, there be made supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, for all men:
Pm
V2
Tfor kings, and all who are in authority, that a quiet and peaceable life we may lead in all piety and gravity,
Pm
V3
Tfor this [is] right and acceptable before God our Saviour,
Pm
V4
Twho doth will all men to be saved, and to come to the full knowledge of the truth;
Pm
V5
Tfor one [is] God, one also [is] mediator of God and of men, the man Christ Jesus,
Pm
V6
Twho did give himself a ransom for all—the testimony in its own times—
Pm
V7
Tin regard to which I was set a preacher and apostle—truth I say in Christ, I do not lie—a teacher of nations, in faith and truth.
Pm
V8
TI wish, therefore, that men pray in every place, lifting up kind hands, apart from anger and reasoning;
Pm
V9
Tin like manner also the women, in becoming apparel, with modesty and sobriety to adorn themselves, not in braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or garments of great price,
Pm
V10
Tbut—which becometh women professing godly piety—through good works.
Pm
V11
TLet a woman in quietness learn in all subjection,
Pm
V12
Tand a woman I do not suffer to teach, nor to rule a husband, but to be in quietness,
Pm
V13
Tfor Adam was first formed, then Eve,
Pm
V14
Tand Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been deceived, into transgression came,
Pm
V15
Tand she shall be saved through the child-bearing, if they remain in faith, and love, and sanctification, with sobriety.
C3
Pm
V1
TStedfast [is] the word: If any one the oversight doth long for, a right work he desireth;
Pm
V2
Tit behoveth, therefore, the overseer to be blameless, of one wife a husband, vigilant, sober, decent, a friend of strangers, apt to teach,
Pm
V3
Tnot given to wine, not a striker, not given to filthy lucre, but gentle, not contentious, not a lover of money,
Pm
V4
This own house leading well, having children in subjection with all gravity,
Pm
V5
T(and if any one his own house [how] to lead hath not known, how an assembly of God shall he take care of?)
Pm
V6
Tnot a new convert, lest having been puffed up he may fall to a judgment of the devil;
Pm
V7
Tand it behoveth him also to have a good testimony from those without, that he may not fall into reproach and a snare of the devil.
Pm
V8
TMinistrants—in like manner grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not given to filthy lucre,
Pm
V9
Thaving the secret of the faith in a pure conscience,
Pm
V10
Tand let these also first be proved, then let them minister, being unblameable.
Pm
V11
TWomen—in like manner grave, not false accusers, vigilant, faithful in all things.
Pm
V12
TMinistrants—let them be of one wife husbands; the children leading well, and their own houses,
Pm
V13
Tfor those who did minister well a good step to themselves do acquire, and much boldness in faith that [is] in Christ Jesus.
Pm
V14
TThese things I write to thee, hoping to come unto thee soon,
Pm
V15
Tand if I delay, that thou mayest know how it behoveth [thee] to conduct thyself in the house of God, which is an assembly of the living God—a pillar and foundation of the truth,
Pm
V16
Tand, confessedly, great is the secret of piety—God was manifested in flesh, declared righteous in spirit, seen by messengers, preached among nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory!
C4
Pm
V1
TAnd the Spirit expressly speaketh, that in latter times shall certain fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and teachings of demons,
Pm
V2
Tin hypocrisy speaking lies, being seared in their own conscience,
Pm
V3
Tforbidding to marry—to abstain from meats that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those believing and acknowledging the truth,
Pm
V4
Tbecause every creature of God [is] good, and nothing [is] to be rejected, with thanksgiving being received,
Pm
V5
Tfor it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.
Pm
V6
TThese things placing before the brethren, thou shalt be a good ministrant of Jesus Christ, being nourished by the words of the faith, and of the good teaching, which thou didst follow after,
Pm
V7
Tand the profane and old women's fables reject thou, and exercise thyself unto piety,
Pm
V8
Tfor the bodily exercise is unto little profit, and the piety is to all things profitable, a promise having of the life that now is, and of that which is coming;
Pm
V9
Tstedfast [is] the word, and of all acceptation worthy;
Pm
V10
Tfor for this we both labour and are reproached, because we hope on the living God, who is Saviour of all men—especially of those believing.
Pm
V11
TCharge these things, and teach;
Pm
V12
Tlet no one despise thy youth, but a pattern become thou of those believing in word, in behaviour, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity;
Pm
V13
Ttill I come, give heed to the reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching;
Pm
V14
Tbe not careless of the gift in thee, that was given thee through prophecy, with laying on of the hands of the eldership;
Pm
V15
Tof these things be careful; in these things be, that thy advancement may be manifest in all things;
Pm
V16
Ttake heed to thyself, and to the teaching; remain in them, for this thing doing, both thyself thou shalt save, and those hearing thee.
C5
Pm
V1
TAn aged person thou mayest not rebuke, but be entreating as a father; younger persons as brethren;
Pm
V2
Taged women as mothers, younger ones as sisters—in all purity;
Pm
V3
Thonour widows who are really widows;
Pm
V4
Tand if any widow have children or grandchildren, let them learn first to their own house to show piety, and to give back a recompense to the parents, for this is right and acceptable before God.
Pm
V5
TAnd she who is really a widow and desolate, hath hoped upon God, and doth remain in the supplications and in the prayers night and day,
Pm
V6
Tand she who is given to luxury, living—hath died;
Pm
V7
Tand these things charge, that they may be blameless;
Pm
V8
Tand if any one for his own—and especially for those of the household—doth not provide, the faith he hath denied, and than an unbeliever he is worse.
Pm
V9
TA widow—let her not be enrolled under sixty years of age, having been a wife of one husband,
Pm
V10
Tin good works being testified to: if she brought up children, if she entertained strangers, if saints' feet she washed, if those in tribulation she relieved, if every good work she followed after;
Pm
V11
Tand younger widows be refusing, for when they may revel against the Christ, they wish to marry,
Pm
V12
Thaving judgment, because the first faith they did cast away,
Pm
V13
Tand at the same time also, they learn [to be] idle, going about the houses; and not only idle, but also tattlers and busybodies, speaking the things they ought not;
Pm
V14
TI wish, therefore, younger ones to marry, to bear children, to be mistress of the house, to give no occasion to the opposer to reviling;
Pm
V15
Tfor already certain did turn aside after the Adversary.
Pm
V16
TIf any believing man or believing woman have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the assembly be burdened, that those really widows it may relieve.
Pm
V17
TThe well-leading elders of double honour let them be counted worthy, especially those labouring in word and teaching,
Pm
V18
Tfor the Writing saith, 'An ox treading out thou shalt not muzzle,' and 'Worthy [is] the workman of his reward.'
Pm
V19
TAgainst an elder an accusation receive not, except upon two or three witnesses.
Pm
V20
TThose sinning, reprove before all, that the others also may have fear;
Pm
V21
TI testify fully, before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the choice messengers, that these things thou mayest keep, without forejudging, doing nothing by partiality.
Pm
V22
TBe laying hands quickly on no one, nor be having fellowship with sins of others; be keeping thyself pure;
Pm
V23
Tno longer be drinking water, but a little wine be using, because of thy stomach and of thine often infirmities;
Pm
V24
Tof certain men the sins are manifest beforehand, leading before to judgment, and certain also they follow after;
Pm
V25
Tin like manner also the right works are manifest beforehand, and those that are otherwise are not able to be hid.
C6
Pm
V1
TAs many as are servants under a yoke, their own masters worthy of all honour let them reckon, that the name of God and the teaching may not be evil spoken of;
Pm
V2
Tand those having believing masters, let them not slight [them], because they are brethren, but rather let them serve, because they are stedfast and beloved, who of the benefit are partaking. These things be teaching and exhorting;
Pm
V3
Tif any one be teaching otherwise, and do not consent to sound words—those of our Lord Jesus Christ—and to the teaching according to piety,
Pm
V4
The is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and word-striving, out of which doth come envy, strife, evil-speakings, evil-surmisings,
Pm
V5
Twranglings of men wholly corrupted in mind, and destitute of the truth, supposing the piety to be gain; depart from such;
Pm
V6
Tbut it is great gain—the piety with contentment;
Pm
V7
Tfor nothing did we bring into the world—[it is] manifest that we are able to carry nothing out;
Pm
V8
Tbut having food and raiment—with these we shall suffice ourselves;
Pm
V9
Tand those wishing to be rich, do fall into temptation and a snare, and many desires, foolish and hurtful, that sink men into ruin and destruction,
Pm
V10
Tfor a root of all the evils is the love of money, which certain longing for did go astray from the faith, and themselves did pierce through with many sorrows;
Pm
V11
Tand thou, O man of God, these things flee, and pursue righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, meekness;
Pm
V12
Tbe striving the good strife of the faith, be laying hold on the life age-during, to which also thou wast called, and didst profess the right profession before many witnesses.
Pm
V13
TI charge thee, before God, who is making all things alive, and of Christ Jesus, who did testify before Pontius Pilate the right profession,
Pm
V14
Tthat thou keep the command unspotted, unblameable, till the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Pm
V15
Twhich in His own times He shall shew—the blessed and only potentate, the King of the kings and Lord of the lords,
Pm
V16
Twho only is having immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable, whom no one of men did see, nor is able to see, to whom [is] honour and might age-during! Amen.
Pm
V17
TThose rich in the present age charge thou not to be high-minded, nor to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who is giving to us all things richly for enjoyment;—
Pm
V18
Tto do good, to be rich in good works, to be ready to impart, willing to communicate,
Pm
V19
Ttreasuring up to themselves a right foundation for the time to come, that they may lay hold on the life age-during.
Pm
V20
TO Timotheus, the thing entrusted guard thou, avoiding the profane vain-words and opposition of the falsely-named knowledge,
Pm
V21
Twhich certain professing—concerning the faith did swerve; the grace [is] with you. Amen.
B2TI 2 Timothy
C1
Pm
V1
TPaul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, according to a promise of life that [is] in Christ Jesus,
Pm
V2
Tto Timotheus, beloved child: Grace, kindness, peace, from God the Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord!
Pm
V3
TI am thankful to God, whom I serve from progenitors in a pure conscience, that unceasingly I have remembrance concerning thee in my supplications night and day,
Pm
V4
Tdesiring greatly to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that with joy I may be filled,
Pm
V5
Ttaking remembrance of the unfeigned faith that is in thee, that dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that also in thee.
Pm
V6
TFor which cause I remind thee to stir up the gift of God that is in thee through the putting on of my hands,
Pm
V7
Tfor God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind;
Pm
V8
Ttherefore thou mayest not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but do thou suffer evil along with the good news according to the power of God,
Pm
V9
Twho did save us, and did call with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace, that was given to us in Christ Jesus, before the times of the ages,
Pm
V10
Tand was made manifest now through the manifestation of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who indeed did abolish death, and did enlighten life and immortality through the good news,
Pm
V11
Tto which I was placed a preacher and an apostle, and a teacher of nations,
Pm
V12
Tfor which cause also these things I suffer, but I am not ashamed, for I have known in whom I have believed, and have been persuaded that he is able that which I have committed to him to guard—to that day.
Pm
V13
TThe pattern hold thou of sound words, which from me thou didst hear, in faith and love that [is] in Christ Jesus;
Pm
V14
Tthe good thing committed guard thou through the Holy Spirit that is dwelling in us;
Pm
V15
Tthou hast known this, that they did turn from me—all those in Asia, of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes;
Pm
V16
Tmay the Lord give kindness to the house of Onesiphorus, because many times he did refresh me, and of my chain was not ashamed,
Pm
V17
Tbut being in Rome, very diligently he sought me, and found;
Pm
V18
Tmay the Lord give to him to find kindness from the Lord in that day; and how many things in Ephesus he did minister thou dost very well know.
C2
Pm
V1
TThou, therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that [is] in Christ Jesus,
Pm
V2
Tand the things that thou didst hear from me through many witnesses, these things be committing to stedfast men, who shall be sufficient also others to teach;
Pm
V3
Tthou, therefore, suffer evil as a good soldier of Jesus Christ;
Pm
V4
Tno one serving as a soldier did entangle himself with the affairs of life, that him who did enlist him he may please;
Pm
V5
Tand if also any one may strive, he is not crowned, except he may strive lawfully;
Pm
V6
Tthe labouring husbandman it behoveth first of the fruits to partake;
Pm
V7
Tbe considering what things I say, for the Lord give to thee understanding in all things.
Pm
V8
TRemember Jesus Christ, raised out of the dead, of the seed of David, according to my good news,
Pm
V9
Tin which I suffer evil—unto bonds, as an evil-doer, but the word of God hath not been bound;
Pm
V10
Tbecause of this all things do I endure, because of the choice ones, that they also salvation may obtain that [is] in Christ Jesus, with glory age-during.
Pm
V11
TStedfast [is] the word: For if we died together—we also shall live together;
Pm
V12
Tif we do endure together—we shall also reign together; if we deny [him], he also shall deny us;
Pm
V13
Tif we are not stedfast, he remaineth stedfast; to deny himself he is not able.
Pm
V14
TThese things remind [them] of, testifying fully before the Lord—not to strive about words to nothing profitable, but to the subversion of those hearing;
Pm
V15
Tbe diligent to present thyself approved to God—a workman irreproachable, rightly dividing the word of the truth;
Pm
V16
Tand the profane vain talkings stand aloof from, for to more impiety they will advance,
Pm
V17
Tand their word as a gangrene will have pasture, of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus,
Pm
V18
Twho concerning the truth did swerve, saying the rising again to have already been, and do overthrow the faith of some;
Pm
V19
Tsure, nevertheless, hath the foundation of God stood, having this seal, 'The Lord hath known those who are His,' and 'Let him depart from unrighteousness—every one who is naming the name of Christ.'
Pm
V20
TAnd in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth, and some to honour, and some to dishonour:
Pm
V21
Tif, then, any one may cleanse himself from these, he shall be a vessel to honour, sanctified and profitable to the master—to every good work having been prepared,
Pm
V22
Tand the youthful lusts flee thou, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace, with those calling upon the Lord out of a pure heart;
Pm
V23
Tand the foolish and uninstructed questions be avoiding, having known that they beget strife,
Pm
V24
Tand a servant of the Lord it behoveth not to strive, but to be gentle unto all, apt to teach, patient under evil,
Pm
V25
Tin meekness instructing those opposing—if perhaps God may give to them repentance to an acknowledging of the truth,
Pm
V26
Tand they may awake out of the devil's snare, having been caught by him at his will.
C3
Pm
V1
TAnd this know thou, that in the last days there shall come perilous times,
Pm
V2
Tfor men shall be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, proud, evil-speakers, to parents disobedient, unthankful, unkind,
Pm
V3
Twithout natural affection, implacable, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, not lovers of those who are good,
Pm
V4
Ttraitors, heady, lofty, lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God,
Pm
V5
Thaving a form of piety, and its power having denied; and from these be turning away,
Pm
V6
Tfor of these there are those coming into the houses and leading captive the silly women, laden with sins, led away with desires manifold,
Pm
V7
Talways learning, and never to a knowledge of truth able to come,
Pm
V8
Tand, even as Jannes and Jambres stood against Moses, so also these do stand against the truth, men corrupted in mind, disapproved concerning the faith;
Pm
V9
Tbut they shall not advance any further, for their folly shall be manifest to all, as theirs also did become.
Pm

Pm

Pm
V13

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm

Pm
V20

Pm

Pm
V23

Pm

Pm
V25

Pm
V26

Pm
V27

Pm
V1

V4

Pm

Pm
V13

Pm
V15

Pm

Pm
V17

Pm
V18

Pm
V20

Pm
V21

Pm
V22

Pm
V23

Pm
V24

Pm
V25

Pm
V26

Pm
V1

B2PE 2 Peter
C1
Pm
V1
TSimeon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who did obtain a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:
Pm
V2
TGrace to you, and peace be multiplied in the acknowledgement of God and of Jesus our Lord!
Pm
V3
TAs all things to us His divine power (the things pertaining unto life and piety) hath given, through the acknowledgement of him who did call us through glory and worthiness,
Pm
V4
Tthrough which to us the most great and precious promises have been given, that through these ye may become partakers of a divine nature, having escaped from the corruption in the world in desires.
Pm
V5
TAnd this same also—all diligence having brought in besides, superadd in your faith the worthiness, and in the worthiness the knowledge,
Pm
V6
Tand in the knowledge the temperance, and in the temperance the endurance, and in the endurance the piety,
Pm
V7
Tand in the piety the brotherly kindness, and in the brotherly kindness the love;
Pm
V8
Tfor these things being to you and abounding, do make [you] neither inert nor unfruitful in regard to the acknowledging of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Pm
V9
Tfor he with whom these things are not present is blind, dim-sighted, having become forgetful of the cleansing of his old sins;
Pm
V10
Twherefore, the rather, brethren, be diligent to make stedfast your calling and choice, for these things doing, ye may never stumble,
Pm
V11
Tfor so, richly shall be superadded to you the entrance into the age-during reign of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Pm
V12
TWherefore, I will not be careless always to remind you concerning these things, though, having known them, and having been established in the present truth,
Pm
V13
Tand I think right, so long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up in reminding [you],
Pm
V14
Thaving known that soon is the laying aside of my tabernacle, even as also our Lord Jesus Christ did shew to me,
Pm
V15
Tand I will be diligent that also at every time ye have, after my outgoing, power to make to yourselves the remembrance of these things.
Pm
V16
TFor, skilfully devised fables not having followed out, we did make known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but eye-witnesses having become of his majesty—
Pm
V17
Tfor having received from God the Father honour and glory, such a voice being borne to him by the excellent glory: 'This is My Son—the beloved, in whom I was well pleased;'
Pm
V18
Tand this voice we—we did hear, out of heaven borne, being with him in the holy mount.
Pm
V19
TAnd we have more firm the prophetic word, to which we do well giving heed, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, till day may dawn, and a morning star may arise—in your hearts;
Pm
V20
Tthis first knowing, that no prophecy of the Writing doth come of private exposition,
Pm
V21
Tfor not by will of man did ever prophecy come, but by the Holy Spirit borne on holy men of God spake.
C2
Pm
V1
TAnd there did come also false prophets among the people, as also among you there shall be false teachers, who shall bring in besides destructive sects, and the Master who bought them denying, bringing to themselves quick destruction,
Pm
V2
Tand many shall follow out their destructive ways, because of whom the way of the truth shall be evil spoken of,
Pm
V3
Tand in covetousness, with moulded words, of you they shall make merchandise, whose judgment of old is not idle, and their destruction doth not slumber.
Pm
V4
TFor if God messengers who sinned did not spare, but with chains of thick gloom, having cast [them] down to Tartarus, did deliver [them] to judgment, having been reserved,
Pm
V5
Tand the old world did not spare, but the eighth person, Noah, of righteousness a preacher, did keep, a flood on the world of the impious having brought,
Pm
V6
Tand the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah having turned to ashes, with an overthrow did condemn, an example to those about to be impious having set [them];
Pm
V7
Tand righteous Lot, worn down by the conduct in lasciviousness of the impious, He did rescue,
Pm
V8
Tfor in seeing and hearing, the righteous man, dwelling among them, day by day the righteous soul with unlawful works was harassing.
Pm
V9
TThe Lord hath known to rescue pious ones out of temptation, and unrighteous ones to a day of judgment, being punished, to keep,
Pm
V10
Tand chiefly those going behind the flesh in desire of uncleanness, and lordship despising; presumptuous, self-complacent, dignities they are not afraid to speak evil of,
Pm
V11
Twhereas messengers, in strength and power being greater, do not bear against them before the Lord an evil speaking judgment;
Pm
V12
Tand these, as irrational natural beasts, made to be caught and destroyed—in what things they are ignorant of, speaking evil—in their destruction shall be destroyed,
Pm
V13
Tabout to receive a reward of unrighteousness, pleasures counting the luxury in the day, spots and blemishes, luxuriating in their deceits, feasting with you,
Pm
V14
Thaving eyes full of adultery, and unable to cease from sin, enticing unstable souls, having an heart exercised in covetousnesses, children of a curse,
Pm
V15
Thaving forsaken a right way, they did go astray, having followed in the way of Balaam the [son] of Bosor, who a reward of unrighteousness did love,
Pm
V16
Tand had a rebuke of his own iniquity—a dumb ass, in man's voice having spoken, did forbid the madness of the prophet.
Pm
V17
TThese are wells without water, and clouds by a tempest driven, to whom the thick gloom of the darkness to the age hath been kept;
Pm
V18
Tfor overswellings of vanity speaking, they do entice in desires of the flesh—lasciviousnesses, those who had truly escaped from those conducting themselves in error,
Pm
V19
Tliberty to them promising, themselves being servants of the corruption, for by whom any one hath been overcome, to this one also he hath been brought to servitude,
Pm
V20
Tfor, if having escaped from the pollutions of the world, in the acknowledging of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, and by these again being entangled, they have been overcome, become to them hath the last things worse than the first,
Pm
V21
Tfor it were better to them not to have acknowledged the way of the righteousness, than having acknowledged [it], to turn back from the holy command delivered to them,
Pm
V22
Tand happened to them hath that of the true similitude; 'A dog did turn back upon his own vomit,' and, 'A sow having bathed herself—to rolling in mire.'
C3
Pm
V1
TThis, now, beloved, a second letter to you I write, in both which I stir up your pure mind in reminding [you],
Pm
V2
Tto be mindful of the sayings said before by the holy prophets, and of the command of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour,
Pm
V3
Tthis first knowing, that there shall come in the latter end of the days scoffers, according to their own desires going on,
Pm
V4
Tand saying, 'Where is the promise of his presence? for since the fathers did fall asleep, all things so remain from the beginning of the creation;'
Pm
V5
Tfor this is unobserved by them willingly, that the heavens were of old, and the earth out of water and through water standing together by the word of God,
Pm
V6
Tthrough which the then world, by water having been deluged, was destroyed;
Pm
V7
Tand the present heavens and the earth, by the same word are treasured, for fire being kept to a day of judgment and destruction of the impious men.
Pm
V8
TAnd this one thing let not be unobserved by you, beloved, that one day with the Lord [is] as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day;
Pm
V9
Tthe Lord is not slow in regard to the promise, as certain count slowness, but is long-suffering to us, not counselling any to be lost but all to pass on to reformation,
Pm
V10
Tand it will come—the day of the Lord—as a thief in the night, in which the heavens with a rushing noise will pass away, and the elements with burning heat be dissolved, and earth and the works in it shall be burnt up.
Pm
V11
TAll these, then, being dissolved, what kind of persons doth it behove you to be in holy behaviours and pious acts?
Pm
V12
Twaiting for and hasting to the presence of the day of God, by which the heavens, being on fire, shall be dissolved, and the elements with burning heat shall melt;
Pm
V13
Tand for new heavens and a new earth according to His promise we do wait, in which righteousness doth dwell;
Pm
V14
Twherefore, beloved, these things waiting for, be diligent, spotless and unblameable, by Him to be found in peace,
Pm
V15
Tand the long-suffering of our Lord count ye salvation, according as also our beloved brother Paul—according to the wisdom given to him—did write to you,
Pm
V16
Tas also in all the epistles, speaking in them concerning these things, among which things are certain hard to be understood, which the untaught and unstable do wrest, as also the other Writings, unto their own destruction.
Pm
V17
TYe, then, beloved, knowing before, take heed, lest, together with the error of the impious being led away, ye may fall from your own stedfastness,
Pm
V18
Tand increase ye in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ; to him [is] the glory both now, and to the day of the age! Amen.

Pm

Pm
V5

Pm
V7

Pm
V8

Pm
V9

Pm
V10

Pm
V11
TBeloved, be not thou following that which is evil, but that which is good; he who is doing good, of God he is, and he who is doing evil hath not seen God;
Pm
V12

Pm
V13

Pm
V14

Pm
V1

Pm
V2

Pm
V3
TBeloved, all diligence using to write to you concerning the common salvation, I had necessity to write to you, exhorting to agonize for the faith once delivered to the saints,
Pm
V4

Pm
V5

Pm
V6

Pm
V7

Pm
V8
TIn like manner, nevertheless, those dreaming also the flesh indeed do defile, and lordship they put away, and dignities they speak evil of,
Pm
V9
Tyet Michael, the chief messenger, when, with the devil contending, he was disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring up an evil-speaking judgment, but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee!'
Pm
V10
Tand these, as many things indeed as they have not known, they speak evil of; and as many things as naturally (as the irrational beasts) they understand, in these they are corrupted;
Pm
V11

Pm
V12
TThese are in your love-feasts craggy rocks; feasting together with you, without fear shepherding themselves; clouds without water, by winds carried about; trees autumnal, without fruit, twice dead, rooted up;
Pm
V13

Pm
V14

Pm
V15

Pm
V16
TThese are murmurers, repiners; according to their desires walking, and their mouth doth speak great swellings, giving admiration to persons for the sake of profit;
Pm
V17
Tand ye, beloved, remember ye the sayings spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ:
Pm
V18
Tthat they said to you, that in the last time there shall be scoffers, after their own desires of impieties going on,
Pm
V19
Tthese are those setting themselves apart, natural men, the Spirit not having.
Pm
V20
TAnd ye, beloved, on your most holy faith building yourselves up, in the Holy Spirit praying,
Pm
V21
Tyourselves in the love of God keep ye, waiting for the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ—to life age-during;
Pm
V22
Tand to some be kind, judging thoroughly,
Pm
V23
Tand some in fear save ye, out of the fire snatching, hating even the coat from the flesh spotted.
Pm
V24
TAnd to Him who is able to guard you not stumbling, and to set [you] in the presence of His glory unblemished, in gladness,
Pm
V25
Tto the only wise God our Saviour, [is] glory and greatness, power and authority, both now and to all the ages! Amen.
